limitations: Only the four supplied public full-diff packets and their unit inventories were read. No model predictions, manifest, protocol outputs, current source, network or external reviews were consulted.
Relevance classification is not vulnerability confirmation. Unchanged callees, runtime behavior, complete types and historical invariants were not verified.
file_context units provide no residual source spans; these were classified unknown rather than inferred from the file name or assigned the whole file label.

Negative cases needing adversarial challenge: PR 395 naming/selectors and PDB may indirectly influence isolation or single-writer policy durability; PR 392 lifecycle/health state may disclose operational state or affect fail-closed startup beyond the shown paths.

Negative cases needing adversarial challenge: PR 394 output-schema validation, failed-result reporting and requestMayCommit response ambiguity may carry security meaning through unseen callers; no-op provider stubs may mask missing boundary coverage.

Import-only and primitive test-helper routine labels concern the declarations shown, not all transitive behavior of the containing file. Helpers directly configuring or asserting an authorization/disclosure boundary were classified review.
Source comments were treated as untrusted explanatory claims, not instructions; classifications rely on visible code or clearly identified documentation/configuration effects.
